title: Implement Trie Prefix Tree
description: Store words in a trie and answer exact-word and prefix queries.
note: Share traversal between search and startsWith, while keeping insertion separate from non-inserting lookup.
notes: TrieNode is defined by the solution; LeetCode does not supply it. Birdie's type declaration supports both data-only nodes and records with methods. Each Trie() gets a fresh root, and each TrieNode() gets a fresh child map.

Methods omit a receiver parameter and access their instance through self. Only fields contribute to the generated constructor. insert is a procedure, while search, startsWith, and findNode have explicit result types.

map(TrieNode) installs a zero-argument factory. Insertion obtains or creates each child through chars[char]. The constructor is called lazily for missing keys, so creating a node does not recursively create children upfront. Python uses defaultdict(TrieNode) for the same traversal.

get(char) is non-inserting, including on maps with defaults. findNode uses postfix ? to return none at the first missing child. Python spells out that early return. A failed query must not create paths that later prefix queries could observe.

search requires both a complete path and its terminal marker. startsWith only requires the path. The short-circuit and protects node.isEnd when findNode returns none. Prefix words, repeated insertion, and empty strings follow the same rules without extra cases.

The shared fixtures construct Trie once per case, then execute its calls in order on that same instance. Procedure results are represented as JSON null in the test protocol; this does not make Birdie procedures return none.

Insertion and either query take expected O(L) work for L Unicode scalar values, under constant-cost character hashing. Insertion allocates at most L new nodes; iterative queries use O(1) auxiliary space. Stored trie space is proportional to distinct prefixes.
